report.title: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5, first public Mythos-class model
report.summary: Claude Fable 5 launched June 9 — the first publicly available Mythos-class model, priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. It leads nearly every benchmark including ~80% on SWE-Bench Pro, ships with hard safety blocks for cybersecurity and bio, and falls back to Opus 4.8 for flagged requests. Free on Pro/Max/Team plans only through June 22; usage-credit billing kicks in June 23.

report.title: Anthropic moves Claude Agent SDK and headless usage to separate metered credit today
report.summary: Starting today (June 15), Claude Agent SDK, claude -p, Claude Code GitHub Actions, and third-party agents exit subscription pools and draw from a new dollar-denominated monthly credit ($20 Pro / $100 Max 5x / $200 Max 20x) billed at API rates with no rollover. Teams running production CI pipelines or autonomous agents need to claim their credit and decide on overflow settings now.

report.title: Claude Code gains nested sub-agents up to 5 levels deep
report.summary: Claude Code v2.1.170 ships nested sub-agent spawning (up to 5 levels), smarter Bedrock region handling, new plugin search, and post-session hooks. The same release introduced Fable 5 access and fixed a long-standing VS Code terminal transcript bug.

report.title: Microsoft ships GitHub Copilot desktop app at Build 2026
report.summary: The GitHub Copilot app launched in technical preview at Build 2026 (June 2-3) for Windows and Mac — a native agent dashboard where each session runs in its own Git worktree, parallel agents can work without collision, and the Copilot SDK is now GA in Node, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java. Requires an existing Copilot subscription; free-tier access promised later.

report.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash is now the default in all Google products; Pro still MIA
report.summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash became the mandatory default in Gemini Enterprise on June 8 — no opt-out toggle remains. It is GA in the API at $1.50/$9 per million tokens. Gemini 3.5 Pro was announced at I/O on May 19 with Pichai promising 'next month,' but has not shipped as of June 15.

report.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.4 absorbs Codex capabilities; GPT-4.5 retiring June 27
report.summary: GPT-5.4 rolled into the main OpenAI lineup consolidating GPT-5.3-Codex agentic coding skills — hitting 75% on OSWorld-Verified computer use, surpassing the human baseline for the first time. GPT-4.5 retires June 27 and o3 retires August 26; teams still on either model need to migrate.

report.title: Gemini API ships Managed Agents in public preview
report.summary: Google launched Managed Agents in the Gemini API — stateful, autonomous agents that run inside secure Google-hosted Linux sandbox environments. Builders get persistent state and isolation without managing their own infra. Event-driven Webhooks for the Batch API also shipped, replacing polling.

learn.name: Claude Fable 5 API
learn.oneLineDescription: Anthropic's first public Mythos-class model via API — top SWE-Bench Pro scores.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Fable 5 (model ID: claude-fable-5) is Anthropic's most capable publicly available model, sitting in a new Mythos-class tier above Opus 4.8. It ships with a 1M-token context window by default and leads nearly every major benchmark — including approximately 80% on SWE-Bench Pro — especially on long-horizon agentic coding tasks. Anthropic reports that early customers used it to complete a Stripe-scale code migration in one day that would have taken a human team two months.

The model includes hard safety blocks for cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry: flagged requests fall back to Opus 4.8 silently. Anthropic also enforces 30-day data retention on all Mythos-class traffic — on both first- and third-party surfaces — so factor that into your data handling review before deploying for enterprise customers. Distillation-attempt detection is active and will also reroute to Opus 4.8.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers and product teams building agentic coding pipelines, long-horizon task runners, or complex knowledge-work automation. If your workload already stresses Claude Opus 4.8 on multi-step reasoning or large-codebase refactors, this is the direct upgrade path. Note: Fable 5 is included on Pro/Max/Team plans at no extra charge only through June 22 — after that it requires usage credits billed at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.
pros: State-of-the-art on SWE-Bench Pro (~80%) and most other agentic coding benchmarks
1M token context window included by default — no suffix needed in the model ID
Drop-in replacement via API; same Anthropic SDK, just swap the model string
cons: 30-day mandatory data retention for all Mythos-class traffic — a compliance consideration for sensitive workloads
Priced at 2x Opus 4.8 ($10/$50 per million tokens); high-volume pipelines will see material cost increases
Hard safety fallback to Opus 4.8 in cybersecurity/bio/chemistry domains — no override available for general users
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Anthropic API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`)
- `anthropic` Python SDK ≥ 0.28 or `@anthropic-ai/sdk` npm ≥ 0.24
- Paid plan (Pro, Max, Team, or API) — Fable 5 is not on Free

## Python quickstart

```bash
pip install --upgrade anthropic
```

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-fable-5",          # exact model ID
    max_tokens=4096,
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Refactor this Python module to use async/await throughout and add type hints."
        }
    ]
)

print(message.content[0].text)
```

## TypeScript quickstart

```bash
npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk
```

```typescript
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

const client = new Anthropic(); // reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env

const message = await client.messages.create({
  model: 'claude-fable-5',
  max_tokens: 4096,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Audit this repo for SQL injection vulnerabilities.' }],
});

console.log(message.content[0]);
```

## Claude Code CLI (terminal access)

```bash
# Update Claude Code to get Fable 5 access
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest  # must be >= 2.1.170

# Verify version
claude --version

# Start a session with Fable 5 explicitly
claude --model claude-fable-5
```

## Gotcha
Model IDs with a `[1m]` suffix (e.g. `claude-fable-5[1m]`) are **automatically normalized** — you do not need to include the suffix. The 1M context is always on.

After June 22, 2026, using Fable 5 on a subscription plan requires usage credits to be enabled in your account settings at console.anthropic.com. Without that toggle, calls will return a 402 error.

learn.name: GitHub Copilot SDK
learn.oneLineDescription: Build custom tools and extensions for the new GitHub Copilot agent desktop app.

detail.whatItDoes:
The GitHub Copilot SDK shipped GA at Build 2026 alongside the new GitHub Copilot desktop app (technical preview). The SDK lets you write custom tools — called extensions — that agents in the Copilot app can call during a session. It supports Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java. Each agent session in the desktop app runs in its own Git worktree so parallel agents don't stomp each other's working trees.

The Copilot CLI was also redesigned at Build: it now supports voice mode and a tabbed terminal interface giving direct access to pull requests, issues, and gists without leaving the shell.
detail.whoItsFor: Platform engineers and developer tooling teams who want to extend GitHub Copilot with internal APIs, deployment scripts, or custom code quality checks. Teams already using Copilot Enterprise who want to migrate toward the new agent-native desktop experience. Requires an active GitHub Copilot subscription (Individual, Business, or Enterprise).
pros: SDK is GA across 6 languages — not a preview, production-ready integration surface
Worktree-per-session isolation prevents agent state bleed in parallel workloads
Native GitHub context (issues, PRs, repos) available to agents without extra auth setup
cons: Desktop app itself is still technical preview — not yet recommended for production agent orchestration
Copilot subscription required; no free-tier access to the app yet (waitlist only)
Windows-only for the desktop app at launch on ARM; Linux support is preview-grade

learn.name: Gemini API Managed Agents
learn.oneLineDescription: Stateful autonomous agents running in Google-hosted Linux sandboxes — no infra to manage.

detail.whatItDoes:
Managed Agents is a new Gemini API primitive (public preview) that lets you deploy stateful, autonomous agents into secure, isolated Google-hosted Linux sandbox environments. The agent persists state across turns, can run shell commands, and connects to your tools via the standard Gemini function-calling schema. Google handles the sandbox lifecycle, so you don't need to provision containers or manage session state yourself.

Alongside Managed Agents, the Gemini API also shipped event-driven Webhooks for the Batch API, replacing the need to poll long-running operations. The File Search API was updated to support multimodal search — you can now embed and search images natively using the gemini-embedding-2 model.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers evaluating Google's agent stack as an alternative to self-hosting agent runtimes. Teams already on Vertex AI or Google Cloud who want a serverless path to persistent agentic workflows without standing up their own sandbox infra. Early-stage products where managing container orchestration for agents is premature.
pros: Google-managed Linux sandboxes eliminate container orchestration overhead for agentic workflows
Persistent state across turns is built-in — no external session store required
Webhook support for Batch API removes polling loops from long-running agent jobs
cons: Public preview — APIs and pricing not yet stable; expect breaking changes before GA
Sandbox environment is Google-controlled; custom OS packages or kernel-level tools are not supported
No self-hosted or on-prem option — all execution stays in Google Cloud
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Google Cloud project with Gemini API enabled
- `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or Application Default Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`)
- `google-generativeai` Python SDK ≥ 1.10 (adds Managed Agents support)

```bash
pip install --upgrade google-generativeai
```

## Define and deploy a Managed Agent

```python
import google.generativeai as genai
import os

genai.configure(api_key=os.environ["GOOGLE_API_KEY"])

# Define a tool the agent can call
def run_tests(test_path: str) -> dict:
    """Run pytest on the given path inside the sandbox."""
    import subprocess
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["pytest", test_path, "--tb=short", "-q"],
        capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    return {"stdout": result.stdout, "returncode": result.returncode}

# Create a Managed Agent (stateful, sandboxed)
agent = genai.ManagedAgent(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",          # or gemini-3.1-pro-preview
    tools=[run_tests],
    system_instruction="You are a CI assistant. When given a repo path, run the tests and summarize failures.",
)

# Start a session — state persists across .send() calls
session = agent.start_session()
response = session.send("Run tests in /workspace/src/api and fix any import errors you find.")
print(response.text)

# Continue the same session (state is preserved in Google's sandbox)
response2 = session.send("Now run tests again and confirm they pass.")
print(response2.text)
```

## Webhook setup for Batch API (replaces polling)

```python
# Register a webhook endpoint before submitting a batch job
batch_job = genai.BatchJob.create(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    requests=[...],
    webhook_url="https://your-service.example.com/webhooks/gemini",
)
# Your webhook receives a POST when the job completes — no polling needed
print(batch_job.name)  # projects/YOUR_PROJECT/locations/us-central1/batchJobs/abc123
```

## Gotcha
Managed Agents are in **public preview** — the request/response schema for `Interactions API` changed on May 26, 2026 (`outputs → steps`). If you pulled early preview code before that date, update to the new schema or your calls will break after the legacy schema was removed on June 8.

learn.name: OpenClaw
learn.oneLineDescription: Local AI gateway connecting frontier models to 50+ integrations — data never leaves your machine.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenClaw is an open-source personal AI assistant and local gateway that connects AI models to over 50 integrations including WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, and iMessage — all running entirely on your own hardware. It acts as a local proxy: your model API keys and all message data stay on your machine, never transiting a third-party server. The project went viral in January 2026 (surging from 9k to 60k stars in days) and has since crossed 210k stars on GitHub.

OpenClaw supports routing requests to multiple backends — OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, local llama.cpp instances — and lets you configure per-integration system prompts, memory, and tool access. It ships with a web UI for managing connections and monitoring traffic.
detail.whoItsFor: Privacy-conscious builders and power users who want AI assistance across their messaging stack without routing data through a cloud intermediary. Engineers who need a local AI router for internal tooling — especially teams with compliance requirements that prevent sending business data to third-party AI providers. Works well as a home lab project or small-team productivity multiplier.
pros: Zero cloud dependency for message routing — all data stays local by design
50+ prebuilt integrations covering every major messaging platform
Backend-agnostic: swap between OpenAI, Anthropic, or local Ollama models per integration
cons: Requires running a persistent local process — not suitable for mobile-only setups or machines that sleep frequently
Integration quality varies; some connectors (iMessage on non-Mac) require workarounds
No official managed hosting option — you own the ops
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS (Apple Silicon recommended for local model acceleration) or Linux
- Node.js 20+ and npm
- At least one AI backend configured: OpenAI API key, Anthropic API key, or Ollama running locally

## Install OpenClaw

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/psteinberger/openclaw.git
cd openclaw

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Copy the example config
cp config.example.json config.json
```

## Configure your first AI backend in config.json

```json
{
  "backends": [
    {
      "id": "anthropic-fable",
      "provider": "anthropic",
      "model": "claude-fable-5",
      "apiKey": "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
    },
    {
      "id": "local-llama",
      "provider": "ollama",
      "model": "llama3",
      "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434"
    }
  ],
  "integrations": [
    {
      "type": "telegram",
      "botToken": "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}",
      "defaultBackend": "anthropic-fable"
    },
    {
      "type": "slack",
      "botToken": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}",
      "appToken": "${SLACK_APP_TOKEN}",
      "defaultBackend": "local-llama"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Start the server

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=... npm start

# Web UI available at http://localhost:3131
# Monitor active integrations, message logs, and backend routing from the dashboard
```

## Gotcha
The iMessage integration only works on macOS and requires granting Full Disk Access to the Node process in System Settings → Privacy & Security. On Apple Silicon, if you're routing to a local Ollama instance, set `"baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:11434"` (not `localhost`) to avoid a DNS resolution delay on first request.
